title: A Hall That Stays Cool
transcript:
Residents in Brookfield will have a new place to escape the heat this summer. From next Monday, the town hall will remain open until ten in the evening on days when the temperature reaches thirty degrees. The hall already has an efficient cooling system, but it normally closes before many people return from work. A local survey found that several apartment buildings stayed hot long after sunset.

The council considered handing out electric fans. However, the health team pointed out that some residents could not afford the additional electricity. Keeping one public building open would provide a cool space without increasing their bills. Visitors will find drinking water, chairs, and a quiet room where children can read. They will not need to book a place or prove where they live.

Volunteers will help people find their way around, while trained staff will handle any health concerns. The council is asking residents to bring their own water bottles, although cups will be available. The main entrance has steps, so signs will direct wheelchair users to the level entrance beside the car park.

The arrangement will run for six weeks. Staff will record the busiest hours rather than simply count daily visitors. This information will help the council decide whether other buildings should offer the same evening service next year.

questions.prompt: Why will the town hall stay open later?
options: Many homes remain hot during the evening.
The cooling system only works at night.
questions.answer: Many homes remain hot during the evening.
questions.explanation: 调查发现一些公寓在日落后仍然很热，而市政厅原本在居民下班前就关闭。

questions.prompt: Why did the council decide against relying on electric fans?
options: The fans would be difficult to deliver.
Some residents could not afford extra electricity.
The town had too few electrical shops.
Most apartments already had new fans.
questions.answer: Some residents could not afford extra electricity.
questions.explanation: 卫生团队指出，部分居民承担不起使用电风扇带来的额外电费。

questions.prompt: Where should wheelchair users enter the hall?
options: Through the level entrance by the car park.
Through a gate behind the gardens.
questions.answer: Through the level entrance by the car park.
questions.explanation: 正门有台阶，指示牌会引导轮椅使用者走停车场旁的平坦入口。

questions.prompt: What information will staff collect during the trial?
options: The electricity bills of nearby homes.
The number of water bottles people bring.
The hours when the hall is busiest.
questions.answer: The hours when the hall is busiest.
questions.explanation: 工作人员将记录哪些时段最繁忙，用于判断其他建筑是否应提供晚间服务。
